recent.title: Great lightweight racer, but snug in the forefoot
recent.text:
The Brooks Hyperion Elite 5 delivers an exceptional upper that locks down seamlessly and truly fits like a glove. Out of the box, the shoe feels remarkably lightweight and nimble on foot, making turnover feel effortless at pace.
The ride is stable and efficient, though the midsole geometry and foam response feel noticeably more controlled and less aggressive compared to high-bounce racers like the Nike Alphafly or ASICS Metaspeed Sky series. It provides a grounded, steady pop rather than a dramatic forward launch.
The only drawback is the forefoot volume—it runs quite narrow, which causes some tightness across wider feet during longer efforts. If you have standard to narrow feet and want a secure, featherlight race-day option with balanced stability, it’s a solid performer.

Overall, the Brooks Vanguard Shoe functions as advertised, however I have one minor issue with it. The outsole (the part of the shoe that comes into contact with the ground) is not as durable as I would have hopped for. After ~2.5 weeks of use, the small rubber circles have worn down a significant amount, leaving the outsole near flat. This reduces your traction making you more prone to falling. Comparing this to other lifestyle shoes I own, like the heavily popular Adidas Sambas, their outsoles do not suffer from this issue. For reference, I usually walk on grass/dirt, concrete, or asphalt. Also I rarely drag my feet or perform athletic activities (skate boarding, dance, run/jog, etc) in these shoes. 

My suggestion is to replace the current outsole with a more durable material so its more on par with its competition. I really hope Brooks addresses this as I think this is the only real issue with the Vanguard shoes. If this is fixed, I will consider buying more pairs.

recent.title: Reinschlüpfen. Passt! Komfort trifft Dynamik. Vom ersten Kilometer an wohlgefühlt. Viel Komfort und trotzdem Dynamik, wenn ich sie haben will.
recent.text:
Der Hyperion Max 3 ist für mich einer dieser seltenen Laufschuhe, bei denen man reinschlüpft und eigentlich sofort das Gefühl hat: passt.

Gerade die Passform finde ich außergewöhnlich gut. Bei vielen Laufschuhen beschäftige ich mich anfangs immer wieder mit der Schnürung, bis wirklich alles sitzt. Beim Hyperion Max 3 hatte ich dieses Thema überhaupt nicht. Gefühlt würde er fast ohne Schnürung funktionieren. 😉

Was mir besonders gefällt, ist die Kombination aus Komfort, Dämpfung und trotzdem richtig guter Dynamik. Die Nylonplatte war für mich dabei auch eine bewusste Entscheidung, weil ich nicht auf Carbon gehen wollte. Sie bringt für mich spürbar Vortrieb, ohne dass sich der Schuh unnötig aggressiv anfühlt oder Wade, Knie und Achillessehne übermäßig fordert.

Und dafür muss man auch nicht permanent unter 5 min/km unterwegs sein. Gerade bei normalen GA1- und GA2-Läufen empfinde ich ihn als sehr komfortabel und habe trotzdem das Gefühl, dass etwas nach vorne geht. Für klassische Tempoeinheiten greife ich zwar lieber zu einem noch leichteren und kompromissloseren Schuh, aber für lockere Läufe und Long Runs ist der Hyperion Max 3 mittlerweile mein absoluter Favorit. Auch im Wettkampf werde ich ihn demnächst einsetzen.

Ganz bewusst habe ich mich übrigens für den Max 3 und nicht für den Nachfolger entschieden. Mir gefällt der reduzierte, etwas race-orientiertere Aufbau des Obermaterials beim 3er ausgesprochen gut. Gerade diese Verbindung aus minimalistischem Aufbau und so viel Komfort finde ich extrem gelungen.

Für einen zukünftigen Hyperion Max würde ich mir wünschen, dass Brooks wieder etwas stärker in diese Richtung geht – gerne auch verbunden mit etwas weniger Gewicht.

Für mich insgesamt ein unglaublich gelungener Laufschuh.

Inserted my orthotics which seemed to have a little more room in the Max 4.  The length and width were exactly what I ordered and fit perfectly.  They felt great inside on carpeted floor and tile.

Out I go for a walk and right away I had a problem...there is less cushioning for the balls of the feet.  I loved the three earlier versions of the Ghost Max series for the cushioning but this model is different.  I gave the shoes a little longer in case it was just a break-in issue but it did not get any better.

I requested a return since there is no way Ghost Max 4 was going to work for me.  At the same time I found that Ghost Max 3 models were still available.  I quickly ordered a pair in my size and will wait for the Ghost Max 5 where hopefully the ball of foot cushioning is restored.

recent.title: Frustrating Shoe
recent.text: Like many others, I am a loyal Brooks runner. I purchased the 3 through a small local running store about a month ago after wearing the Max for the last year. I don't like or need so much cushioning, so I was really excited and have tried so hard to like them. I love the color (turquoise blue with pink), but most of the other options are boring and uninventive. I want my shoes to stand out. But, the overly large soles are starting to look ridiculous (on every brand). The sock tongue works for me, because it keeps it from sliding and the laces are stretchy and don't come untied. however, the toe box is noticeably smaller than the previous model, so my toes stick together and develop blisters. I am also baffled by the "padding" around the achilles. It's too much and not soft. It literally has caused bruising and pain. Why does it need to be so tight? And so high up the ankle? It squeezes and pushes the foot forward, so that when I take the shoe off, I still feel like I'm wearing it. I keep trying to stretch and soften the padding, but it's not getting any better. I'm ready to take scissors to it. It's too late for me to return these, so I'm stuck with my worn down Hyperion Max. I'm frustrated from the experience,  I agree with other reviewers: don't make changes just for the sake of making them and don't make so many at once. Sometimes, less is better. Hoping for a better Hyperion 4.

recent.title: Fast Pace Running Shoe
recent.text: I'm transitioning from beginner to immediate runner, taking it up in my late 40s, so I don't have a ton of experience with running shoes yet. So far, On Cloudmonster has worked best for me, but because the cushioning doesn't last more than 3 or 4 months, I'm trying different brands and shoes and that's how I landed on the Hyperion Max 3. It was recommended through the shoe finder feature and has really strong reviews. After 2 runs, totaling 9 miles, they are breaking in and feeling better little by little. Overall, I think this is my first true race shoe. This shoe wants you to go fast! It gears you toward running on your fore foot and the bounce is so pronounced, it more comfortable to go at a faster pace than a daily pace. I range between 10:30 and 12:30 depending on various factors. These shoes have kept me at 11:30 or better for the two runs - whether I like it or not! I've also noticed significant arch support. There are 2 issues for me: the narrow toe box means my pinkie toes go numb about 1/3 of the way into the run. Also, I tend to pronate to the outside of my forefoot and there's no support for that in these shoes like with the cloudmonsters. I don't think it's a sizing issue - the length still leaves room beyond my toes (8.5 is my size in Brooks). I plan to keep these as a race shoe for 5Ks and my first 10K, knowing they will continue to feel better with each run. Final note on the aesthetics - it's a sharp looking, beautiful shoe! I also like the stealthfit upper that reminds me of the Glycerin. It fits super snug around the ankles, so don't stress about tying the laces tightly.

Unfortunately, the sizing is not the same as for the running shoes - my Ghost trail runner is visibly narrower than my Glycerin, especially in the toe box, though they both say they are 9 D.  The Ghost is also visibly significantly longer.  I thought my foot would slide around due to its length, but it doesn’t because the outer toes hit the shoe when I walk because it is so narrow,  However, as I work to break them in, something that is not necessary with my Glycerins which are immediately comfortable at purchase, I’m finding it causes soreness on the outer edges of my feet and the very tips of my toes.  Also the tongue on the left side seems to dig into the top of my foot for some reason, but not on the right.  On the plus side, the traction is good and the moderate cushioning on the foot bed provides much greater comfort than the Cascadias that I have also tried in the past but which made me feel every pebble underfoot.  In short, if I was an M/C width I would order a D and it might work very well and if a DD is added to the lineup in the future I might give it a try. recent.title: Great short for speed sessions on the track
recent.text: The Brooks Dash Speed Short is a fantastic warm weather short for hard sessions on the track. They are also a great option for racing up to a 10k if you have an outside option for storing your house/car key. These shorts push the threshold for being as minimal as possible with a 3” inseam, mesh paneling and split sides, and zero additional features. It appears that Brooks took the Breakaway 3” short and added split sides and removed the small interior and left hip pockets. The polyester fabric of the Dash Speed Short feels slightly thicker than the Breakaway short and the waist runs a little larger though. Having the little extra room in the waist of my size medium short is definitely appreciated for my 32” inch waist as they feel like they are sized perfectly. Another huge plus is that the material for the waist is extremely comfortable. These shorts are super lightweight and breathable and feel like you have nothing on outside of the liner. They are perfect for warm days on the track as long as you have a safe place to stash your keys. The split sides give an extremely airy feel, but be warned that the sides will flap and can reveal the outside of your backside. I have a thicker rear end than most men with my waist size (from 30+ years of playing ice hockey), so it is likely these shorts are simply more revealing for me. For that reason, I would only recommend these to someone who feels confident with their body image. I’m fairly comfortable with shorter running shorts, so the Dash Speed Short will be a go to short for me during my track workouts in the hot and humid summers in the DMV area.

recent.title: Surprisingly warm, light, breathable jacket
recent.text:
The Movement Relaxed jacket is a really nice jacket for runs and walks. The jacket is extremely light weight and thin, which honestly made me nervous at first (I got it for cooler fall/winter runs/walks). However, this jacket is just what I needed. 

The jacket is true to size if you notice the “relaxed” part of the title. I’m a bigger guy, and got the same size I usually get, and there’s plenty of room in the jacket, without it feeling too flowy or long. Sometimes to get this relaxed feeling you have to size up, and you end up with sleeves that are just a bit too long or a length that doesn’t work, but that’s not the case here. Great relaxed fit without looking too baggy.

The fabric is thin and doesn’t irritate or wear you down, even over long runs. It’s made of a stretchy material that looks almost like it’s a tight-knit mesh. What surprises me most is that for how thin it is, it retains heat really well. I thought I’d have to move to a heavier duty jacket as the temperatures got lower and lower, but for most days I can still get by with long sleeve running base layer and this jacket on top. The pockets have zippers to keep things secure if you use them. The only design choice I’m still not sold on is the flap around the mid-section of the jacket. Sometimes flaps like this have mesh under for added breathability, but I think on this jacket it’s purely aesthetic. It looks fine, but doesn’t necessarily add to the functionality. 

Overall, this jacket was great on daily walks and runs, very breathable when sweating and hot while still helping regulate temperature for cooler days. This jacket is great!

I'm gonna start with my favorite part - I can fit a soft flask in the front pocket without it bouncing or feeling awkward! Results may vary but I found that for a 500ml flask filled 80% (that's 400ml of fluid) it feels secure enough to race, which I did!

I only buy tights with brief liners now, and these are a great option in a market that has a lot of cheaper options that require a $30 pair of underwear underneath. My normal size small fit true to size and they are easy enough to out on. My thighs and rear end are probably a medium but my waist is a small, and the small works great for me without feeling restrictive. 

The material is quite soft and seamless along the bottom edges, which is nice because some tights start to dig into my legs a bit at the bottom end if there's a seam. These aren't constructed with the most lightweight material you'll ever see but they're versatile enough for all seasons for me. 

The thickness almost knocked my rating down to a 4, but the storage capacity brought it back to a 5/5. Phone can go in the rear zipper pocket or either of the side leg pockets. You can stash a ton of gels or even some fluids in the front pocket, which notably has a secure point midway along the width of the pocket which makes access a little tougher but keeps things from falling out accidentally.

recent.title: Not made for anyone who's gone through pregnancy or values breathing deeply
recent.text:
I cannot begin to describe just how much I hate this trend of Brooks' sewing inch-wide elastic that's tighter than the tights themselves into the top of a high-rise compression waistband. The core is a pressure management system that extends from the pelvic floor to the roof of the mouth, and that elastic is like putting a rubber band around the middle of a balloon, rendering it unable to inflate and deflate properly. In my 20s, I would have found it uncomfortable for running but probably would have lived with it; as someone with diastasis recti postpartum in my 40s, absolutely not.

In addition to the interior elastic (sewn in, I've tried on other similar tights to cut the waistband open with the thought of cutting out the elastic, and you can't do it without taking the whole waistband apart and then sewing it back together), the drawstring is flimsy. Size L fit me perfectly except for the elastic and was otherwise very comfortable - if it weren't for the elastic, I would have kept and probably loved them. Size XL was way too big and I had to cinch the drawstring all the way to get an okay fit through the waist and was afraid I was going to snap the drawstring trying to get it tight enough. 

This is the second pair of tights I've ordered from Brooks this year to find this added elastic in without it being mentioned in the product description, and I'm done with Brooks tights for a while as a result.

recent.title: Awesome workout and summer time shirt

I love Brooks Running products! I have several shoes and shirts, which are durable, lightweight, and comfortable. Recently, I had the chance to try the High Point Short Sleeve 2.0 shirt. The timing is perfect to try this now that summer is here and it is warming up.
 
The shirt is lightweight, very breathable, and keeps me cool. The fit is semi fitted, which allows me to freely move unrestricted, yet not too loose or baggy. I like the reflective logo details which help keep me visible when the sun starts to set.
 
The shirt is fuchsia, with two dark blue accent panels on the side. It looks great and I’ve gotten several compliments. The fabric is very lightweight and soft on my skin. It is a very fine mesh fabric, but not see-through.
 
Overall, I love how the shirt fits, allows full motion, and keeps me cool on hot days. I appreciate the fabric is wrinkle free and I can wear it casually. Brooks really nailed the design and fabric of this shirt. I highly recommend it!

recent.title: When You move, it moves with you!
recent.text:
The Brooks Graphic tank, even after several washes, this tank stays incredibly soft and flexible. The fit around my arms is comfortably made but fitted enough to feel flattering, but never restrictive. It gives me freedom to run, stretch, and move with trust, that the brand that I wear will not fail, and keep me focused where I need to be. I truly believe that what you wear affects how you feel. What I love the most is its versatility. This isn't just a running sleeveless tank for the gym or the outdoors. The Brooks graphic tank is stylish enough to switch your game to running errands and be comfortable enough for your all-day wear. I did find it slightly fitted, so sizing up could be an option, but honestly, the fit is still comfortable enough to make me motivated to work harder. When I feel comfortable, confident, and unrestricted, I am inspired to push harder and stay consistent with my goals. This top doesn't just support my runs, it supports my mindset. 
If you're looking for comfort, flexibility, and motivation in one piece of activewear, this graphic tank delivers. I have definitely recommend it to my friends and family.

recent.title: PR Elite Split Short
recent.text:
I have been wearing the Brooks PR Elite Split Short in a size Small. In hindsight, I would likely choose a Medium next time. I tried the mid-rise fit, and while it wasn’t uncomfortable at all, it did feel a bit snug around my love handles. For my body type, sizing up would probably provide a slightly more relaxed fit.

The fabric feels extremely lightweight and smooth on the run, with no irritation or chafing. It moves well with the body and never felt restrictive, even at faster paces. One standout feature for me was the built-in lightweight brief liner — it was supportive and comfortable, and I honestly forgot it was there while running, which is always a good sign. I also appreciated the small key pocket on the right-hand side of the inner lining, which was a convenient and thoughtful detail.

Overall, the shorts performed very well on daily runs. They stayed in place, handled sweat effectively, and felt breathable throughout. Aside from my personal sizing preference, I was very happy with the comfort and performance of these shorts — they truly made me feel like a professional.

recent.title: Best Running Tights
recent.text: I’ve struggled to find running shorts that don’t bunch or ride up. These Cascadia Short Tights were the most comfortable fit I’ve ever had. There was hardly any movement when running due to the raw hem design around the legs. An added benefit of that design was also that it didn’t cut into my thigh at all. It was a perfect fit. The waist was just the right amount of compression without digging in. There is an internal drawstring but I didn’t need to utilize it. The length was perfect- not too short, not too long. I loved all the pockets and storage options- zipper pocket on the back, side leg pocket and even waist belt pockets to easily slip in whatever you want to bring along. The advantage of having these pockets attached to your shorts is no extra bouncing waist belt or arm band. I found these shorts to be a flattering, true to size fit. The material was comfortable and thick enough to avoid any “see through” effect with bending/ stretching. I absolutely love these shorts and won’t be running in anything else!
